Subject: MSA + DPA redlines for pilot

Hi Jasmine / Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — the pilot looks promising. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and the DPA (MSA+DPA redline v3). Our procurement team needs to confirm the hosting/jurisdiction language and whether you can accept the standard SCCs we use. Key asks from our side:

- Confirm controller/processor roles remain as in the draft and provide the subprocessor roster.
- Confirm whether you can commit to EU SCCs + a transfer impact addendum for EEA data.
- Clarify KMS ownership and options for customer-managed keys for the pilot.
- We will need audit log access and a list of retention settings.

Can you confirm a timeline? Procurement needs an executed contract + PO by 21 Dec to meet internal start dates. DocuSign link will follow once we agree redlines.

Attachments: CloudHealth_MSA_DPA_redline_v3.docx, CloudHealth_PO_5678.pdf

Thanks,

Thanks Ellen — received and we’ll coordinate internally. Looping in Legal (Laura) and Privacy/Ops (Monica) to triage the redlines. A few quick clarifications for procurement so we can prioritize:

- Is the PO you attached strictly conditional on accepting all redlines, or can we present a fall-back variant (MSA with DPA + limited transfer addendum)?

1) Legal & Privacy will review the redlines today (internal target EOD 18 Dec).

If the timeline is tight, Ben — can you confirm commercial flexibility if we need to offer a 30-day pilot-specific addendum (short term transfer addendum + limited SLA exception)?

Thanks — Jasmine

Subject: Re: MSA + DPA redlines for pilot — internal legal summary

Jasmine / Ben — quick internal summary after an initial read of CloudHealth's redlines:

1) Roles & Liability: The redline attempts to shift more controller obligations to Redwood in clause 2. We should push back and re-assert processor responsibilities as in our standard DPA.
2) SCCs & Transfers: They want standard EU SCC modules and an explicit transfer impact addendum. We can accept SCCs but will need a transfer-addendum that:
   - Limits transfer scope to pilot data types (an explicit annex),
   - Includes a defined notice-and-mitigation workflow for export requests, and
   - Disallows automatic subprocessor delegation without customer notice for EEA data.
3) KMS: CMK for pilot is operationally heavy. Proposed compromise: provide Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) for a single customer-managed key under a pilot fee; otherwise use Redwood-managed KMS with contractual encryption commitments.
4) Audit & Logs: Provide a scoped audit bundle (logs + sampling) on a quarterly cadence for pilot; full streaming audit access is a commercial uplift.
5) Subprocessors: We'll provide current roster and commit to 30-day notice before adding new subprocessors; limit onshore-only hosting cannot be promised for the pilot without an orderform-level surcharge.

Action items (internal):
- Ben: confirm pricing headroom / pilot discount and whether PO timeline is firm.
- Monica: assemble subprocessor roster and retention defaults, and confirm what we can include in the transfer addendum annex.
- Jasmine: coordinate with Ellen on negotiable items and confirm DocuSign timeline.

I will prepare redline comments and a proposed transfer-addendum template by EOD 19 Dec.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA + DPA redlines for pilot — commercial note

Team — quick commercial position:

- We can accept the SCCs and a pilot-scoped transfer addendum if we (a) limit the scope to production/non-sensitive telemetry for the initial 90-day pilot, and (b) add a 15% pilot discount and an orderform surcharge for any onshore-only hosting requirement.
- If CloudHealth insists on CMK for the pilot, we need a $7,500 setup fee + $2,000/mo ops uplift; otherwise Redwood-managed KMS is included.

Ben — can you push this to procurement and ask if the PO is flexible? If they insist on a full, unrestricted transfer addendum without commercial uplift we should flag to Legal.

— Ben Carter

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement confirmed the PO is contingent on an executed agreement by COB 21 Dec, but they can accept a pilot-scoped transfer addendum if it includes:

- Explicit annex limiting EEA transfer scope to the pilot dataset and a 30-day review window;
- SCCs applied with the standard EEA modules and a commitment to provide subprocessor roster;
- Agreement on KMS: procurement prefers CMK but can accept Redwood-managed KMS if we include the audit bundle and crypto controls statement.

We are comfortable with the 15% pilot discount and the onshore hosting surcharge model (procurement will sign off if costs are capped and visible on the orderform). Please send the redlined counter by noon PST so we can route to our legal/ops and push DocuSign.
